lines.description: Ordered lines. Array order is presentation order.

cast.description: Who each speaker in this scene actually is, stated once for the scene rather than repeated on every line. Each entry names a speaker string exactly as the lines spell it and the unit type whose character that speaker is, and a client that draws a face draws the same character the board draws for that unit type: the same style, the same figure, the same archetype and the same faction colour. It says nothing about the words: the speaker string stays exactly what it is, and a speaker called 'Evil Dragon' still reads 'Evil Dragon'. Presentation only: no rule reads it and it never enters the canonical state hash. A speaker no entry names, and a scene with no cast at all, is drawn the way each client drew a speaker before a scene could name one.

speaker.description: The speaker string this entry is about, matched against a line's own speaker exactly and case-sensitively. Spell it the way the lines spell it.

unitTypeId.description: The unit type whose character this speaker is. A reference into this project's unitTypes.

backgroundId.description: What this scene is drawn against, chosen from the backdrops the art library provides. A backdrop is a run of flat horizontal bands rather than a picture, so it costs no client a texture; a client with too few colours for the bands draws the one colour the backdrop names as its wash. It belongs to the scene rather than to the story node, so a cutscene that moves from the hall to the wall names two. Presentation only: no rule reads it and it never enters the canonical state hash. Omit it and the scene is drawn on the flat fill each client already used, which is what a scene looked like before backdrops existed.
